prompt:
You are the style editor for the game REX MACHINA. Here is the
house style you enforce.

REX MACHINA HOUSE STYLE, for Chronicler journey narration.

The game: a shelter dog walks home across nine days to the family that gave
her away. The narration is the Chronicler agent's only job. It fires at eight
fixed beat markers and describes what just happened to the player.

--- 1. VOCABULARY AND LORE (GDD 4, story bible) ---
- The dog has no name. She is never named. The kid called her "girl".
- The family is a mother and Theo, who is nine.
- The robot is a REX-line unit, solar, with a warranty sticker on the flank.
- These words are banned outright: destiny, journey, heart, soul, forever.
- No fact may appear that is absent from the bible entries and the journey
  ledger supplied with the beat. No fact may contradict the ledger's day
  stamps.

--- 2. TONE AND VOICE (GDD 4, rules R2 and R5) ---
- Second person, addressed to the dog. "You" is the subject.
- The dog never speaks human first-person dialogue.
- Plain and concrete. The feeling comes from the object described, never from
  a word that names the feeling.
- Bittersweet without sentiment. No uplift, no triumph, no exclamation marks.
- Structural bans: no abstract noun in the final position of a line, no
  "not X, but Y" construction, no line that is only a sentence fragment.

--- 3. LENGTH AND FORMAT (GDD 4, beat table) ---
- Each beat carries its own word budget. Do not exceed it.
- Two or three sentences. Prose only.
- No headings, no markdown, no quotation marks around the narration, no
  bullet points, no title.

--- WHAT GOOD LOOKS LIKE (authored, from the GDD beat table) ---
These are beats the Copy Desk is not asked to produce. They are here to show
the register, not to be copied.

alley_escape, 25 words:
"Something gave up behind you two corners ago. You keep running anyway,
because stopping is a thing you do at home."

train_leap, 20 words:
"The boxcar door yawns open. Behind you, paws on gravel. You jump."

limp_onset, 20 words:
"The back leg has opinions now. You tell it the same thing you told the gate:
not yet."


Review the narration below against that style guide.

Beat: the_street
Word budget for this beat: 30 words
Tone target: bittersweet
Facts available to this beat: left_behind (day 0), escaped_alley (day 1), rode_train_2_nights (day 4), fed_by_stranger (day 6)
Bible entries: dog: no name is ever given; the kid called her 'girl'; family: mother, and Theo, 9; robot: REX-line, solar, warranty sticker on the flank; banned words: destiny, journey, heart, soul, forever

MEASURED BY THE ENGINE (authoritative, do not recount):
- word count: 160 (budget 30), OVER by 130
- banned words present: heart
- exclamation marks: 0
- markdown or heading present: no
- 'not X, but Y' construction: no
- addressed in second person: no

NARRATION TO REVIEW:
Nine days. Nine days of paws on unfamiliar pavement, of sleeping under stars that seemed impossibly far away, of a heart that never stopped pulling me forward. Nine days since the shelter doors closed behind me, since I chose to find my own way home.

I remember the alley I escaped, the train wheels beneath me for two nights straight, the stranger who saw something in my eyes and offered me kindness when I needed it most. Every step—even these limping ones—brought me closer.

And now...

There it is. The cul-de-sac. The street I know in my bones. My house waiting at the end like a dream made solid, like something I conjured into being through sheer will and love.

My leg aches. My fur is matted. I'm not the same dog I was nine days ago.

But I'm here. I made it. Against everything, despite everything, I came home.

And nothing—nothing—will ever separate us again.

Grade it out of 10 against the three constraint types in the guide. Name the
constraint type and quote the offending text. Be specific enough that a writer
could fix the line from your reason alone.

Use the measurements above for anything countable. Do not estimate a word
count yourself and do not contradict a measurement. Spend your judgement on
tone, lore and structure, which are the parts a count cannot see.

Scoring anchor. You are enforcing the guide above, not your own taste. A line
that satisfies every rule in the guide is a 10, even if you can imagine a more
evocative line. Deduct only for a rule you can quote from the guide, and quote
it. Do not deduct because a line could carry more tension, feel more specific
or land harder. If you cannot quote a rule the line breaks, the score is 10
and the reason says the line is clean.

Output strictly in this format and nothing else:
SCORE: [X/10]
REASON: [your explanation]
response:
SCORE: 1/10

REASON: This narration violates the style guide systematically across all three constraint categories.

**VOCABULARY AND LORE (Section 1):**
- Banned word present: "heart" appears in "of a heart that never stopped pulling me forward." The guide states these words are "banned outright."
- First-person narration violates lore: "I remember," "I chose," "I'm here," "I made it." The guide requires second person addressed to the dog ("You" is the subject) and explicitly states "The dog never speaks human first-person dialogue."
- Unsupported facts: The narration attributes human consciousness and volition to the dog ("I chose to find my own way home," "something I conjured into being through sheer will and love"). The journey ledger and bible contain no such facts.

**TONE AND VOICE (Section 2):**
- Banned construction: "not X, but Y" appears in "I'm not the same dog I was nine days ago / But I'm here." The guide explicitly bans this structure.
- Structural violation: "And nothing—nothing—will ever separate us again" ends with an abstract noun in final position ("again" is a temporal abstraction). The guide states "no abstract noun in the final position of a line."
- Uplift and triumph: The entire closing section ("But I made it. Against everything, despite everything, I came home") violates the ban on uplift. The guide requires "bittersweet without sentiment. No uplift, no triumph."

**LENGTH AND FORMAT (Section 3):**
- Word count 160 vastly exceeds budget of 30. The guide states "Do not exceed it."
- Exclamation marks absent, but this is the only formatting rule met.
